judgements.reason: target passage (Article 30 only) never mentions slavery, servitude or the slave trade, in any form
no mention of remedies, tribunals or any body charged with enforcing rights; passage only bars interpreting the Declaration as licensing destruction of rights
nothing about penal offences, presumption of innocence, guilt or trials
nothing about movement, residence or State borders
nothing about marriage, spouses or consent
nothing about property or how it may be owned
nothing about social security or a person's capacity as a member of society
nothing about work, remuneration, workers or families
nothing about rest, leisure, working hours or holidays
passage refers to 'the rights and freedoms set forth herein' but never mentions any social or international order, nor any order a person is entitled to
no mention of arbitrary interference, privacy, family, home or correspondence
nothing about freedom of movement, residence or borders
no mention of marriage, race, nationality or religion; the passage lists no grounds of any kind
passage names 'any State' but says nothing about government, its authority or the will of the people
nothing about remuneration, workers, families or human dignity
nothing about motherhood, childhood, care or assistance
no mention of duties, the community or development of personality; passage addresses only interpretation of the Declaration
nothing about torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment
nothing about hearings, equality before a tribunal, or fairness of proceedings
nothing about penal offences or national and international law
nothing about asylum, prosecutions or the purposes and principles of the United Nations
nothing about nationality or the right to change it
no mention of associations or of anything a person may be compelled to belong to; 'group' appears only as a possible actor, not as something one may be compelled to join
nothing about national effort or international co-operation as a means of realizing rights
nothing about pay, work or discrimination
no list of circumstances of insecurity (unemployment, sickness, etc.) exists in the passage
passage does not name morality, public order or general welfare, but it is adjacent: Article 30 is itself a limiting clause on how rights may be invoked
no list of items protected from arbitrary interference appears in the passage
nothing about asylum or persecution
nothing about marriage or consent of intending spouses
nothing about taking part in government, directly or through representatives
nothing about rest, leisure, working hours or paid holidays
no mention of unemployment, sickness, disability, widowhood, old age or lack of livelihood
passage never says limitations are determined 'by law', but it is adjacent: it constrains how the Declaration's rights and freedoms may be invoked
nothing about recognition as a person before the law, nor any statement of where such a right applies
nothing about hearings, rights and obligations being determined, or criminal charges
nothing about penalties or the time an offence was committed
no grounds relating to marriage or founding a family are listed anywhere in the passage, so no count can be given
no mention of property or deprivation of it; the word 'arbitrary' does not appear either
passage mentions 'rights and freedoms' generically but describes no kinds of rights as indispensable for dignity, so no count is available
